climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds plenty of water, which can push leafy, vigorous vines unless growers rein them in. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
